prior_findings.note: Independent probe reproduced it: multipart A(part_index=0)/B(part_index=1) in one conversation, A's transport raised AmbiguousDeliveryError, one drain pass produced outcome=:drained, attempts=["A-part0","B-part1"], durable A=unknown, B=succeeded. tamoz-comms ships no ordering primitive and its CommsStore contract exposes no conversation sequence or predecessor-eligibility operation, so the missing contract is at this row's seam; finding remains owned by F12.

findings.title: truncate overflow discards the remainder with no marker, against the written rendering contract
findings.recommendation: At the existing Rendering.plain seam, append one bounded marker part (or a marker suffix on the last part) when the truncate branch drops characters, naming the thread and `tamoz show`, exactly as design/comms.md:113 already specifies. One branch in split plus one test.
findings.evidence: Probe /tmp/f11/probe_render.rb: 12000 chars, max_parts 3, part_characters 100 -> 3 parts, joined length 300, contains_marker false. comms_rendering_test.rb:35-41 asserts only part length.

findings.title: rendered channel text is never scrubbed or escaped, and the declared render format is validated but never read
findings.recommendation: At the existing Rendering seam, add the escaper the contract already names (restricted_html closed tag set, `&<>` escaped) and have outbox_delivery_sink.rb / gateway_delivery.rb select it from the surface's rendering.format, which they already hold. Keep plain default and unchanged. If unsupported, remove restricted_html from RENDER_FORMATS instead of accepting-and-ignoring it.
findings.evidence: grep across repo: only the constants and the design prose; zero consumers. Probe: \x00 \x07 \x1b[31m \r \t pass through byte-identical; '<b>&<a href=...>' returned unescaped. No test asserts escaping -- not found. Impact graded medium because the shipped adapter sets no parse_mode and no live bot was exercised.

findings.title: binding revocation does not take effect while the correspondent is also on the configured allowlist
findings.recommendation: At Admission.decide's existing binding guard (admission.rb:40), treat a `revoked` binding as terminal for the correspondent rather than as a non-grant, before the allowlist is consulted, using existing :rejected/:unbound vocabulary. One guard reorder plus one admission test.
findings.evidence: admission.rb:97-99 ORs the configured list against the binding, so a revoked binding never vetoes a listed id. comms_store.rb:195-200 revoke_binding is correctly implemented and simply never consulted. No test covers revoked-and-listed -- not found.

findings.title: a channel callback reaches the decision path without any allowlist or pairing check
findings.recommendation: At admission.rb:41, route callbacks through the same allowlist/pairing correspondence check command_admission and text_disposition already use, returning the existing :ignored/:pairing_pending vocabulary, and keep the prompt binding compare as the second independent control. Add one test pressing a callback from an unlisted sender.
findings.evidence: The callback branch short-circuits before both correspondence checks; probe shows an unlisted correspondent sending kind=callback yields :decision under both allowlist and pairing. Impact bounded by gateway_callbacks.rb:35-38 evidence gate and :66-71 binding compare, which currently hold; no test presses a callback from an unadmitted sender -- not found.

findings.title: mark_delivery records any status from any claimed row, so the delivery state machine has no legal-transition guard
findings.recommendation: At the existing CommsStore#mark_delivery contract (comms_store.rb:126-133), state the precondition that a succeeded/unknown outcome applies only to a claimed row whose send boundary marker is set, and add `AND send_started_at_ms IS NOT NULL` to the SQLite UPDATE. One clause, one contract sentence, one drainer test.
findings.evidence: The WHERE guards only status='claimed' plus owner/fence; status is written from the caller's argument. delivery_drainer_test.rb:184-209 asserts only the fence guard. Implementation owned by F07; recorded at this contract's seam.

findings.title: the store never verifies content_digest against the text it persists, so a corrected re-render is silently dropped as a duplicate
findings.recommendation: At the existing append_delivery seam (comms_store.rb:63-70), when the id already exists compare the stored content_digest with the incoming one and return a typed conflict instead of :duplicate when they differ. One comparison in comms_outbox.rb plus one store test.
findings.evidence: Delivery.build validates the digest's shape only; append dedups on id existence. delivery_drainer_test.rb:317-322 builds deliveries with Digest::SHA256.hexdigest(text) rather than Rendering.content_digest and they are accepted and delivered. No test asserts a digest mismatch is refused -- not found.

findings.title: max_response_bytes is written as optional and is actually required, raising an untyped KeyError
findings.recommendation: At surface_descriptor.rb:184, use transport[:max_response_bytes] (or .fetch(..., nil)) so the existing nil tolerance is reachable, or drop the tolerance and validate the key like its siblings. One character of change plus one descriptor test.
findings.evidence: `cap = transport.fetch(:max_response_bytes); return if cap.nil? || ...` -- fetch raises before the nil branch. Probe reproduced `KeyError: key not found: :max_response_bytes` from :184. No test builds a descriptor without the key -- not found.

findings.title: a successful send whose fence was lost leaves its approval prompt permanently inactive with no reason recorded
findings.recommendation: At delivery_drainer.rb:103, when marked != :marked for an approval_request row, record the same reason_code vocabulary already used for the authentication failure (:108-115) so the skipped activation is durable and diagnosable.
findings.evidence: activate_after_receipt runs only when marked == :marked && status == 'succeeded'; no record is emitted on the :not_claimable branch. delivery_drainer_test.rb:184-209 never pairs the stale-owner write with an approval_request row -- not found. The row state itself stays honest (claimed -> unknown by reconciliation), so this is observability only.

findings.title: milestone card lookup scans all succeeded rows for the surface on every push
findings.recommendation: At the existing call site, pass the limit the store already supports and stop after the first match while the newest row still belongs to the reference; or add a request_ref-filtered read to the existing CommsStore outbox reader.
findings.evidence: outbox_rows is called with no limit on every milestone push; the store orders by created_at_ms. Bounded by outbox capacity via admission (comms_store.rb:30-42), hence minor. agent_outbox_delivery_sink_test.rb is small-fixture only -- no bounds assertion found.

info.text: Group chats and unknown kinds are refused twice over: admission.rb:39 and admission.rb:38, with envelope construction permitting those prefixes (inbound_envelope.rb:165-168) but never admitting them.
The thread digest is generation-aware and deterministic (admission.rb:56-61, v2 domain); /new bumps the generation and rotates the thread without deleting audit history.
An allowlisted first contact writes a Binding with bound_by 'gateway:allowlist' (gateway_admission_binding.rb:41-51). The value is truthful and whoami echoes the envelope, so no authority is forged.
restricted_html is dead configuration -- declared and validated at surface_descriptor.rb:37,234-246 and consumed by nothing. Folded into F11-SEC-01.
F12-REL-01 (unknown-ordering) reproduced at HEAD 582ae55 by an independent probe; still open, still confirmed, still owned by F12 with F07/F11 follow-up.

tests_not_run.reason: not found -- the brief's named file does not exist; the store contract is tested by test/sqlite_comms_store_test.rb, which was run

probes.purpose: control characters, escaping, truncation marker, code-fence split, grapheme safety
same-pass ambiguous predecessor with a multipart successor, over the real SQLite store and DeliveryDrainer

blind_spots: No live Telegram endpoint: whether an entity injection or link preview is actually produced from unescaped text is an external fact not exercised; this is why F11-SEC-01 is medium.

tamoz-sqlite comms_store.rb read selectively (admission, append, claim, mark, reconcile, resolve, revoke regions); the projection/status/receipt queries were not read line by line -- row F07 owns them.
tamoz-comms-gateway read for the caller trace only; gateway_answers.rb, gateway_context_controls.rb and gateway_status.rb were skimmed, not audited -- row F12 owns them.
No rake ci/ci_full, RuboCop, Reek, SimpleCov or Enola snapshot; maintainability graded from source and gemspec, not from a lint result.
The delivered_card_message_id and comms_delivery resolve scans were reasoned from source, not measured under a large outbox.
No new concurrency probe; the existing two-drainer and stale-owner tests were run but no additional race was constructed.
